ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), ss. 5, 27-40 and Schedule 2 (financial institution status for issuers and managers of payment instruments); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011, reg. 7 (beneficial ownership threshold); Companies Act 1993, ss. 21-24 (name rules) and ss. 85-89 (shareholder and director registers); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 (mandatory FSPR registration); Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, s. 163 (restricted use of the word bank); supervisory guidance issued by the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA), Financial Markets Authority (FMA), and Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ); New Zealand has not yet enacted a publicly searchable statutory UBO register, and the disclosure of ultimate beneficial ownership is enforced through AML/CFT customer due diligence obligations imposed on reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Apostille member states, including the People's Republic of China (effective since 7 November 2023); consular legalization for any non-member state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, licensed bank, or relevant government authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and banking relationship for each material UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed relationship bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register Extract for any corporate shareholder that is itself an entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or licensed registered agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against (i) the New Zealand consolidated sanctions list maintained under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, the United Nations Act 1946 sanctions regulations, and the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN and SSI lists, adopted as sponsor-bank and international card network commercial standard; (iv) UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists where the entity intends EU or UK cross-border activity; and (v) recognized PEP databases covering domestic and foreign politically exposed persons plus their immediate family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence under AML/CFT Act ss. 29 and 31 is triggered by PEP status, negative adverse media flags, or jurisdiction risk scoring. Screening results must be evidenced, retained for at least five years post-relationship, and refreshed at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register Name Availability Search and Online Name Reservation Portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal company names must be expressed in the Roman alphabet (A-Z); Arabic numerals and permitted punctuation such as hyphens, ampersands, apostrophes, full stops, and spaces are allowed; non-Roman scripts including CJK characters are not accepted in the statutory company name. Macrons used in Te Reo Maori words are acceptable where the transliteration is consistent with the Companies Register system. Every limited liability company must end with the word Limited or the abbreviation Ltd. A proposed name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing registered name, reserved name, or incorporated society name, and must not mislead as to the company's regulated status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is held for 20 working days and may be extended for a further 20 working days by written application to the Registrar of Companies filed before expiry, upon payment of the prescribed fee. Where the Registrar refuses a name on grounds of identity, almost-identity, offensiveness, regulated-words, or misleading connotation, the applicant may file a fresh reservation for a modified name immediately or request administrative reconsideration in writing, attaching legal submissions and evidence of distinctiveness. A reconsideration request should be lodged within 10 working days of refusal. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand within three months of the adverse decision. For regulated financial services names containing tokens such as virtual card or payment, the Companies Office will consult the Financial Markets Authority before approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally acceptable. A New Zealand company must maintain a registered office at a physical address within New Zealand capable of receiving service of documents; a P.O. Box alone is insufficient. A virtual office or registered-agent service address satisfies the Companies Act 1993, but the proposed regulated fintech card issuer must also demonstrate genuine local commercial substance under the AML/CFT Act and Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, including a locally resident AML/CFT compliance officer, operational management, board minutes, accounting records, and an audit trail. A purely virtual arrangement without operational substance will not sustain the statutory license and will be rejected by DIA and FMA during the authorisation review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 70 percent probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months after licensing and commencement of card issuance). DIA and FMA conduct risk-based, largely unannounced inspections of high-risk reporting entities in the digital payment and card issuance segment, requiring immediate production of CDD files, transaction monitoring records, and corporate books.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 10-16 (Incorporation), s 124 (Appointment of Directors), s 126 (Appointment of Secretary), ss 54-57 (Share Capital), s 200 (Registered Office), Schedule 1 (Constitution)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form NZ Companies Register online application), together with the Company Constitution and Consent to Appointment forms
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated under the Companies Act 1993; the company may issue shares with nil paid or nominal consideration, provided that the directors resolve the issue price and any escrow or payment terms in accordance with section 58 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF NZ_LTD. Pursuant to the Companies Act 1993, the directors of NZ_LTD, a company incorporated in New Zealand, hereby resolve as follows: (1) SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: the initial share capital shall be allotted to the subscribers as set forth in the application, and the directors confirm that the consideration for such shares is lawful, that no minimum paid-up capital is required, and that any shares issued on credit terms shall be recorded in the share register in accordance with the Act. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: the registered office of the company shall be established at the address stated in the incorporation application, and the Board shall file any change of address with the Registrar within the prescribed timeframe. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: the individuals named in the consents to appointment are hereby appointed as directors and, where applicable, as the company secretary, each having the powers and authorities conferred by the constitution and the Companies Act 1993. (4) GOVERNANCE: the directors shall open a New Zealand bank account, procure the corporate seal, and cause the company to comply with its tax and filing obligations. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterpart.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and File Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) via the online Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Register; reserve the name 'NZ LTD' if required. Complete the online incorporation application providing the proposed company name, registered office address, director and shareholder details, share structure, and any Constitution. Attach signed consents to appointment. The application is submitted electronically and the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation upon successful validation.
required_dossiers: Completed Incorporation Application
Company Constitution (if adopted)
Consent to Appointment of each director and secretary
Director and shareholder personal information (name, address, date of birth)
Registered office address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant should receive a formal requisition or notice from the Registrar. The applicant must address the stated defects, correct the data, and resubmit via the online portal. In the event of an adverse decision on name approval, a new name may be reserved and the application amended without re-paying the incorporation fee except where additional services are requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute First Board Resolution and Adopt Corporate Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of NZ_LTD; minutes filed with the company records, not the Registrar unless constitution amendment is lodged
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting or obtain a written resolution in accordance with the Companies Act 1993. Resolve the share allotment, adopt the registered office, appoint directors and any company secretary, and set the financial year-end. Record the minutes in the company register and retain originals at the registered office.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Share register and shareholder ledger rollover
Director and secretary consents
Registered office adoption record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or a financial institution queries the board resolution, the directors shall reconvene and execute a confirmatory resolution or corrected minutes and rescind or supersede the defective resolution. Legal counsel may provide a certificate of correctness if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for IRD Number and Register for GST and Provisional Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply for an IRD number using the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and the incorporation details. Determine GST registration requirement based on taxable supply thresholds; register for GST online and select the applicable filing frequency. The IRD will issue the IRD number and GST registration confirmation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN issued by the Companies Office
Directors' personal tax information
Registered office address and business address
Business activities declaration (payment card issuing in scope ISIC 6619)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is delayed or queried, provide the requested supporting information or evidence of business activity through the myIR portal. A tax agent can file a notice and escalate for administrative review. If the taxpayer is not subject to GST, file an exemption notice; if provisional tax obligations arise, request an instalment arrangement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Employer Obligations and Financial Services Provider Register (FSPR) if Required
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department and Financial Markets Authority / FSP Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company employs staff, register as an employer with the IRD for PAYE and KiwiSaver. For the issuance of virtual cards, assess whether the entity must register on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008. Submit the FSPR application online with the Companies Register number and attestations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
IRD number confirmation
Directors' identification documents
Business description and licensing statement
Compliance and dispute resolution scheme membership evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSP registration application is rejected, the applicant may revise the information or appear before the FSP Registrar for review. If the service is regulated by the Financial Markets Authority, the company must obtain the appropriate licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 before commencing regulated activities. Non-material defects can be cured by written representations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Obtain Payment Card Programme Access
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered banks in New Zealand and card network sponsors (e.g. Mastercard or Visa) through the licensed acquiring or issuing bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, open a corporate bank account with a New Zealand incorporated bank. Submit the certificate of incorporation, board resolution, constitutional documents, and director identification and address documentation. Undergo customer due diligence and anti-money laundering vetting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. For card issuing, enter into a card programme agreement with a sponsoring bank that holds membership with the relevant card network.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (colour copy)
First Board Resolution authorising bank account and card programme
Company constitution and corporate governance registers
Director and beneficial owner identity and source-of-funds documents
Proof of registered office and business address
Tax status and financial statements (if any)
Compliance plan and AML programme outline
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account opening due to AML concerns, the applicant may provide an enhanced due diligence pack, correct the compliance plan, and approach an alternate bank. If the card network programme application is delayed, engage with the sponsor's onboarding team, procure a letter of comfort from a qualified principal, and resubmit the application with the correct ISIC and business classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) for business registration; if physical card production is involved, the industrial licensing authority may include the Department of Internal Affairs for physical security aspects, but for virtual card issuance the competent authority is the FMA and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) depending on the payment service scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Advice Provider (if applicable) and Payment Services Licence under the Payment Services Act 2022 (for payment services), or authorisation as a non-bank payment service provider via the Reserve Bank of New Zealand; for physical operations, a general business licence is issued by the local council.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration or exempt from the need for a formal EIA where the activity is limited to virtual card issuance and administrative operations; however, any physical data centre or card personalisation facility may require an assessment under the Resource Management Act 1991 as a Controlled Activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The undertaking must comply with the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards) Regulations and local council plans. For wastewater discharges, compliance with the National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water and the Water Services Act 2021 is required. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from any printing or card personalisation process must not exceed the relevant NES for Air Quality (attainable limits of 250 mg/Nm3 total VOC for stationary sources unless a stricter regional rule applies). E-waste and card waste handling must follow the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the National Environment Standard for Assessing and Managing Contaminants in Soil to protect human health.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004 is required where the entity occupies premises open to employees or clients. Fire safety certification must be provided under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, including an evacuation scheme and fire detection system. Structural load inspections and a safe working certificate are necessary for any office or operational premises. A workplace induction and safety clearance must be obtained from an independent assessor, confirming compliance with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; online portal myIR administered at https://www.ird.govt.nz; corporate registry interface operated by the New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An NZ limited company is first incorporated with the New Zealand Companies Office, which issues the NZBN and automatically notifies Inland Revenue; Inland Revenue then issues the IRD number to the registered company, normally within 10–15 business days. Foreign-owned NZ Ltd entities must ensure compliance with director residency rules under the Companies Act 1993 (at least one director resident in New Zealand or, for large overseas-owned companies, an approved legal or accounting firm acting as agent), and must apply separately for GST registration through myIR if taxable supplies exceed the registration threshold, are reasonably expected to exceed the threshold, or if voluntary registration is desired. Non-resident companies not carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand but deriving New Zealand-source income must apply for an IRD number using form IR 742 (Registration of non-resident company) or equivalent myIR online protocols; the application requires certified constitutional documents, director identity evidence, and details of the New Zealand agent or representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (New Zealand resident company taxed on worldwide income at the corporate rate of 28%, unless validly elected as a look-through company); Territorial_Scope (resident companies are taxed on worldwide income with a foreign income exemption for certain active foreign business income, foreign dividends, and grey-list CFC interests); Pass_Through_Eligible (an NZ Ltd may elect look-through company status so that income, expenses, gains, losses, and GST implications flow through to shareholders in proportion to their effective look-through interests); Tax_Exempt_Zone (not applicable—no general tax-exempt zone status in New Zealand, although certain development projects or specific statutory concessions may apply separately).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Look-Through Company (LTC) election under the Income Tax Act 2007 (form IR 433 or via myIR, subject to shareholder eligibility, no more than five owners, and all shareholders having voting/ownership interests between 5% and 100% of the company considered on a look-through basis); grandfathered Qualifying Company (QC) election for companies that held QC status before the repeal, with a 2011 proxy basis retained for eligible legacy entities; GST grouping election under s 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to treat two or more related companies as a single group for GST purposes; GST payment basis elections (invoice basis, payments basis, or hybrid basis, and the six-monthly filing option); and statutory hybrid mismatch anti-avoidance rules under subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007, which prevent elective neutralisation of hybrid financial instruments and do not provide taxpayer election mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (value-added tax system administered by Inland Revenue)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in taxable supplies (excluding exempt supplies and GST) in any 12-month period for suppliers of goods and services within New Zealand; a NZD 60,000 threshold similarly applies to remote services and digital suppliers above the threshold who must register under the non-resident remote services rules; once registered, GST is payable on taxable supplies and input tax credits are recoverable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping by Inland Revenue. The official New Zealand e-Invoicing network (Peppol-based, operated through accredited access points) is voluntary and available to GST-registered businesses. GST returns and payments are submitted electronically through myIR without an API-based transactional clearance requirement; all suppliers must maintain sufficient source documents to substantiate GST positions. No fiscal digital stamping regime is in force; however, IRD retains the power to require digital record production and access under the Tax Administration Act 1994, and records must be retained for at least 7 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under s 11 of the GST Act 1985, supplies of goods are zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of the time of supply, retains satisfactory evidence of export, and the goods are not subsequently used in New Zealand; services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed are zero-rated under s 11A unless the services are directly in connection with land in New Zealand, goods in New Zealand, or are services of a kind supplied in connection with mines, petroleum, or other natural resources in New Zealand. Remote services supplied to non-resident private consumers may be zero-rated under s 11B where the non-resident recipient is outside New Zealand at the time of supply. Critically, for a B2B virtual card issuer, the issuance of cards, interchange, scheme fees, and transaction-processing services constitute exempt financial services under s 3 of the GST Act 1985; these exempt supplies are generally not zero-rated, and the issuer cannot recover input tax attributable to exempt financial supplies except under the 75%/95% de minimis rules. Only separately invoiced non-financial back-office, software-as-a-service, or consulting services supplied to offshore non-resident customers may qualify for zero-rating under s 11A, provided the recipient is outside New Zealand when the services are performed and no New Zealand land or goods nexus exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZ Customs Export Declaration submitted electronically through the Trade Single Window (a legitimate exporter must obtain an export entry number and customs clearance approval)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods from New Zealand to the overseas destination
Commercial invoice and packing list or service agreement and task completion report executed by the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange receipt showing payment received from the non-resident customer in foreign currency

Non-resident status evidence for services recipients (e.g., certificate of residency, foreign VAT registration number) and contemporaneous records confirming the recipient was outside New Zealand at the time the services were performed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits export zero-rating claims through the GST return and, on challenge, may assess additional GST at 15% of the zero-rated supply value if the statutory zero-rating conditions are not met or the required export documentation is inadequate; clawback adjustments are applied to input tax credits claimed on goods that cease to be exported or are later diverted to New Zealand use, with shortfall penalties ranging from 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or an arrangement to defeat the intent of the GST Act as set out in ss 141A–141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994; criminal prosecution under s 143A (knowingly doing anything that evades GST) imposes fines of up to NZD 50,000 for an individual plus up to NZD 250,000 for a company, and the evasion of tax with intent to defraud may carry imprisonment of up to 5 years; systematic false zero-rating of exempt financial services further exposes the corporate card issuer to use-of-money interest on the assessed shortfall, late filing penalties of NZD 250 per month, and potential disqualification from the GST instalment regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), the apex monetary authority and prudential supervisor for banks, non-bank deposit takers, and payment system settlement infrastructure; foreign exchange administration is not separately delegated, with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervising conduct and disclosure and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) serving as the AML/CFT supervisor for non-bank financial institutions under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalized and freely convertible currency regime for both current account and capital account transactions; the New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a free-floating currency with no statutory exchange control approvals, licensing, or transaction-level permissions for ordinary inwards or outwards treasury flows. Profit and dividend remittances from an NZ limited company are unrestricted under the Companies Act 1993 and the foreign exchange framework, but are subject to statutory Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at 30% or a reduced treaty rate depending on the recipient jurisdiction, and to an anti-money-laundering verification of the underlying transaction purpose. For a corporate virtual card issuer, the genuine convertibility friction is not governmental exchange control but prudential characterisation: overnight holding of cardholder float or stored value can be re-characterised as deposit-taking under the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013 unless the funds are held with and settled through a licensed sponsor bank; all card-related intercompany funding must therefore be supported by board resolutions, signed treasury mandates, and contemporaneous purpose codes to demonstrate that funds are not disguised deposits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline, no surrender obligation, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; the Exchange Control Act 1973 has been repealed and exporters may retain foreign currency offshore indefinitely. The only administrative requirements are the periodic Balance of Payments statistical return thresholds administered through Statistics New Zealand, standard AML/CFT transaction record-keeping, and the banks internal sanctions-related screening policy. For the NZ_LTD virtual card treasury, this means inbound liquidity from the offshore parent can be structured in NZD, USD, EUR, or AUD without any Reserve Bank of New Zealand currency conversion approval, subject only to the receiving bank's internal FX policy, sanctions checks, and source-of-funds verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational NZD/USD Transaction Account
Operational Transaction Account with Foreign Currency Settlement Module
Operational Account with Sponsor-Bank Card Settlement Integration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for a remote offshore EMI passporting into New Zealand; MEDIUM for a locally incorporated sponsor-bank agency structure. New Zealand has no EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) licence and no passporting regime; an entity holding customer funds or stored value must either be a registered bank or a licensed Non-Bank Deposit Taker (NBDT) under the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013, or alternatively must act purely as a program manager with all funds held at a licensed sponsor bank under a contractual trust or agency arrangement. The NZ_LTD virtual card issuer must register on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, join an approved dispute resolution scheme, and appoint a locally resident compliance officer. The Retail Payment System Act 2022 regulates access and pricing of retail card networks but does not create an EMI authorisation; therefore a foreign digital EMI lacking NZ regulatory substance, FSPR registration, and sponsor-bank backing will not be granted clearing or settlement access by tier-1 NZ banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one director with signing authority must appear physically at the bank's corporate banking centre in Auckland or Wellington for the initial board-level KYC interview; remaining directors may join through a recorded video conference facilitated by a qualified NZ law firm. Remote-only onboarding is not available for an AML-high-risk virtual card issuer with an offshore trust ownership chain; the bank will also conduct enhanced due diligence including verification of the beneficial ownership register, source-of-wealth examinations for natural persons, and an on-site session if the NZ entity maintains any office. For the NZ treasury plan, the physical onboarding should be scheduled within 30 days of incorporation, with two directors executing the banking mandate and the NZ-resident compliance officer present, and all corporate documents must be notarised and apostilled in advance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed stored-value or quasi-deposit-taking exposure where the overseas parent sweeps cardholder float into the NZ entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: External legal opinion from an NZ-licensed barrister confirming that the card float does not constitute repayable deposits under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989 or the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013; executed daily fund-sweep agreement with the licensed sponsor bank; RBNZ fit-and-proper notification letter; settlement flow diagrams evidencing that funds remain at the sponsor bank; board resolutions approving the treasury architecture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership where an offshore trust chain conceals the economically exposed individuals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised extract from the NZ Companies Office shareholder register; declaration filed under the beneficial ownership register provisions of the Companies Act 1993 as amended by the Companies (Register of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2023; deed extracts and trustee declarations for each offshore trust layer; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds dossiers for every beneficial owner; tax residence certificates for all natural-person shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and proliferation financing exposure in the merchant acceptance base and cardholder portfolio
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved sanctions screening policy; subscription to the Consolidated New Zealand Sanctions List, OFAC SDN list, and United Nations sanctions lists; merchant category code geo-blocking configuration; express prohibition of cash-equivalents and money-service-business merchants; independent audit report on the transaction monitoring system; documented escalation matrix for suspicious activity reports to the DIA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cash-equivalent card loading with immediate withdrawal patterns inconsistent with expense management
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-programmed spend-control rules including merchant class restrictions and single and aggregate daily limits; real-time transaction monitoring alerts with machine-learning analytics; contractual evidence of the travel-and-expense-only use case with corporate customers; six-monthly customer re-verification programme; suspicious activity reporting protocol compliant with the AML/CFT Act 2009.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border mismatch where cards are issued in New Zealand but settlement instructions point to non-resident accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal treasury mandate and banker's instruction letter signed by all directors; pre-notified SWIFT purpose codes for each settlement batch; monthly reconciliation ledger between card network presentments and bank account movements; sponsor-bank indemnity covering the card network acquiring and issuing licence; FSPR registration certificate and membership certificate of an approved NZ dispute resolution scheme.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial and subsequent equity or subordinated loan injections from the offshore holding structure should be routed as SWIFT MT103 customer transfers (or MT202 if interbank) to the NZ settlement account at the tier-1 sponsor bank, using the New Zealand Balance of Payments purpose code for direct investment equity or intercompany treasury funding; the payment must reference the legal registration number and full registered name of NZ_LTD. Funds received in NZD convert at the interbank spot rate without any Reserve Bank of New Zealand exchange-control approval. The receiving bank will require: a board resolution approving the capital call and investment purpose; certified director identification for the account authority; documentary evidence that the USD or other source currency originated from legitimate operational revenue or committed capital; and for amounts above the ordinary operational threshold, a capital-purpose letter addressing both New Zealand tax substance and screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 exemption for non-sensitive ordinary business securities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Card-as-a-service treasury settlement is executed daily through the sponsor bank to the network schemes using Visa Direct and Mastercard Network clearing and settlement rails, with net positions settled across the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Exchange Settlement Account System (ESIS) at end-of-day. Non-card treasury disbursements to fund approved cardholder vouchers use the BECS Bulk Electronic Clearing System for domestic NZD payments and SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wires; commercial letters of credit are issued under UCP600 through the sponsor-bank trade desk, with documentation checked per ISBP745 and electronic documents accepted under e-UCP wherever the card program crosses borders. Liquidity is consolidated into the NZD operational account at the sponsor bank, with concentration sweeps upstream to the offshore parent restricted by day-end trade posting to avoid unintended deposit-taking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forwards between NZD and USD, AUD, EUR, GBP negotiated under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX Swaps where a spot NZD purchase is paired with an offsetting forward sale for treasury liquidity timing mismatches
Cross-Currency Swaps limited to long-term intercompany funding liabilities and settled through the sponsor bank's collateral arrangements
Vanilla FX Options, both calls and puts, for budget protection on large inbound capital injections without restricting upside

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted only where a counterparty cannot deliver NZD due to jurisdiction restrictions; NDFs are rarely necessary because the NZD is freely deliverable, and any NDF usage must be pre-cleared by the sponsor bank and documented for RBNZ prudential transparency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month after the Annual Return Date, which is the later of the incorporation anniversary and six months after the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZ$100 (approx. USD 62) if filed within 20 working days after the due date; NZ$200 (approx. USD 124) if filed later. Persistent non-filing permits the Registrar to issue a removal notice and strike the company off the New Zealand Register under s.318.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the 7th day of the seventh month after balance date (7 July for a standard 31 March balance date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZ$250 (approx. USD 155) for companies with taxable income above NZ$2 million; nil for small companies. Late payment penalties (1% to 4%) and use-of-money interest accrue on unpaid tax; an unfiled return may trigger a default assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Return, if GST-registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly or six-monthly) is determined by turnover; returns are due by the 28th day of the month following the end of each GST period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZ$250 (approx. USD 155) for non-small businesses. Late payment penalties of 1% immediately, 4% after seven days, and 1% per month thereafter; use-of-money interest applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR), administered by the New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 20 working days after the anniversary of the date of FSP registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under s.37 of the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; fines up to NZ$10,000 (approx. USD 6,200) with continuing contraventions attracting further penalties; removal from the FSPR bars the carrying on of regulated financial services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) supervisor (Reserve Bank of New Zealand or Financial Markets Authority, as designated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the timeframe specified by the supervisor in its annual reporting instructions (typically within three months after balance date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to provide a report is an offence under s.90 of the AML/CFT Act 2009; on conviction a body corporate is liable to a fine up to NZ$2 million (approx. USD 1.24 million); civil penalty orders may also be sought by the supervisor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and Audit Report (if an FMC reporting entity or audit is a licence condition)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (for FMC reporting entities); AML/CFT supervisor or licensing authority for licence-condition audits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after balance date for an FMC reporting entity; otherwise as prescribed by the audit engagement terms for licence-condition audits.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offences and civil penalties under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; late or non-lodgement can result in fines up to NZ$1 million (approx. USD 620,000) plus continuing daily penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory if the company is an FMC reporting entity, is not eligible for the small-company exemption (total assets over NZ$30 million / approx. USD 18.6 million, annual turnover over NZ$15 million / approx. USD 9.3 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees), or if the AML/CFT supervisor or licensing authority imposes an audit condition. Exemption for other companies requires unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (IFRS as adopted in New Zealand) for FMC reporting entities and large for-profit entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) for smaller for-profit entities without public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies Act 1993 there is no separate annual beneficial-ownership return; shareholding changes are recorded in the Register of Members and the Annual Return confirms current members and directors. Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the company must maintain current beneficial-ownership information obtained through customer due diligence and refresh it upon any transfer of shares or change of control. The Companies (Disclosure of Beneficial Ownership) Legislation Act 2023 will, once in force, require a separate beneficial-ownership register to be kept at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges (if any charges exist)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in New Zealand. The R&D Tax Incentive provides a 15% credit on eligible research and development expenditure, and the R&D loss cash-out scheme may provide early monetisation for losses. No preferential rate exists for fintech or virtual card issuing activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 annual company tax return filed electronically via myIR (Inland Revenue's electronic filing system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax paid in three installments during the income year where residual income tax exceeds NZ$5,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: IR4 is due 7 July following the 31 March balance date for electronic filers (or 7 June for paper filers). For non-standard balance dates, due date is the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date for electronic filers. Terminal tax is due 7 April following balance date; provisional tax installments for standard balance dates are due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, IRD number, and registered office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the New Zealand IRD number; where a foreign-incorporated company is carrying on business in New Zealand, also state the overseas tax identification number and country of tax residence.
Standard 31 March balance date unless an approved corresponding income year has been agreed with Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income: all New Zealand-sourced gross income including card scheme rebates, interchange fees, merchant service fees, interest, and software/platform fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only New Zealand-sourced income attributable to a New Zealand fixed establishment or from services performed in New Zealand is taxable. Foreign-source income of a non-resident company is excluded unless derived through a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions: operational costs, payment processing fees, software depreciation, bad debts, management fees, interest and other business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must relate to assessable New Zealand income. Thin capitalisation and interest apportionment rules apply to non-resident-owned companies; transfer pricing adjustments must be made on related-party charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or loss after tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable income using New Zealand tax rules, not foreign GAAP. Apply arm's-length transfer pricing for intra-group service fees.
Apply the 28% corporate rate to taxable income; non-resident withholding tax on dividends or royalties is separate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: imputation credits, RWT on interest, foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be claimed only under a DTA or New Zealand's unilateral foreign tax credit rules and must be supported by overseas tax returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reflect all provisional tax paid. Late payments attract use-of-money interest and penalties.
Only required if the company maintains an imputation credit account to attach credits to dividends. Non-resident shareholders generally cannot use imputation credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties escalate from NZ$250 to NZ$1,000. Late payment penalties: 1% on day 1, additional 4% on day 8, then 1% per month (or 0.5% for terminal tax under installments). Use-of-money interest on underpayments applies at the prescribed rate. Shortfall penalties range from 20% to 150% of the tax shortfall depending on fault, including 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic statutory rate on dividends to non-residents is 30% for non-imputed dividends; 5% applies to fully imputed dividends paid to non-resident companies. Treaty rates may reduce this further (e.g., 15% or 0% depending on DTA and ownership).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced withholding rates, the non-resident payee must provide a valid tax residence certificate from its home jurisdiction, and the payer must retain this document for audit. For dividends, a declaration of non-residence and beneficial ownership is required. For interest and royalties, an IR67 declaration must be completed. Inland Revenue may require an approved issuer levy election where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT 15% on gross royalties; most New Zealand DTAs reduce royalties to 10% (some to 5% for certain cultural/industrial royalties). Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; most DTAs reduce interest to 10%; the approved issuer levy (2%) may apply to non-associated lender interest. Software and technology licensing for virtual card platforms should be carefully structured to avoid deemed royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Transfer pricing documentation (local file/master file equivalent) is expected where cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$10 million per income year. Smaller transactions may still require documentation where they are high-risk or involve significant value. Inland Revenue follows OECD guidelines and may require documentation on demand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No separate New Zealand ESR statute, but the general anti-avoidance rule (section BG 1), OECD Principal Purpose Test, and treaty beneficial ownership requirements force substantive operations. A virtual card issuer must maintain real employees, premises, decision-making, and risk management in New Zealand; otherwise income may be recharacterised and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting interchange revenue, faking expenses, diverting card scheme rebates to offshore accounts, or operating without the required payment services license while issuing virtual cards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994: fines up to NZ$250,000 for a company and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals. Evasion shortfall penalties up to 150% of tax shortfall. Unlicensed payment services offences under AML/CFT Act can attract fines up to NZ$3 million and 2 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns may be personally liable for the tax shortfall; courts may pierce the corporate veil and make civil restitution orders. Travel bans, asset freezing and imprisonment are available under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 and Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length charges for software, card network access, or management fees paid to offshore affiliates; excessive intercompany debt; failure to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may reallocate income and disallow deductions. Shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% of the adjustment apply. Thin capitalisation breaches cause interest deductions to be denied. Failure to provide documents on notice can result in statutory penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign false transfer pricing documentation may be jointly and severally liable; imprisonment up to 5 years for aiding tax evasion. If the company is a facade, the corporate veil can be pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No real operations, no employees, no board meetings; using offshore shell entities to route New Zealand business profits through a low-tax jurisdiction while claiming treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR and Principal Purpose Test will void the arrangement and reallocate income. Penalties up to 150% of tax shortfall; DTA relief denied. Company may be removed from Companies Register for failing to meet substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors behind the sham may be personally liable for corporate tax debts, disqualified from management for up to 5 years, and subject to travel bans and asset restraint orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing virtual cards without proper customer due diligence; failing to report suspicious transactions; operating without registering on the Financial Service Providers Register and obtaining the required license under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 or Payment Systems and Stablecoins Act 2022.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to NZ$3 million for companies and NZ$300,000 for individuals plus 2 years' imprisonment per offence. Licenses may be cancelled and the business shut down. Pecuniary penalties recoverable by the FMA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are individually liable under section 52 AML/CFT Act for failures to implement and maintain compliance programs. Personal pecuniary penalties up to NZ$2 million, imprisonment, and disqualification from directing financial services companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing virtual cards without a principal membership with Mastercard/Visa through an approved licensed institution; acting as payment system operator without regulatory approval; falsely holding out as a bank.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under the Non-bank Deposit Takers Act 2013: fines up to NZ$1.5 million for a company (daily penalties apply). Under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, pecuniary penalties up to NZ$1 million. Consumers can seek restitution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly participating in unlicensed activity are personally liable for penalties, can be disqualified for up to 5 years, and may face imprisonment up to 3 years where fraud is involved. Travel bans and asset freezing orders available.
